summary: Facility-location covering-set selection over pooled individual questions
hypothesis: Pooling individual questions across multiple adapter draws and selecting 7 via a submodular facility-location / max-dispersion objective should surface rare critical unknowns that appear in only one low-temperature draw, because the embedding-distance term would promote questions far from the modal cluster into the final set.
technique: Over-generate a pool of ~28 individual questions from the champion adapter (1 greedy draw + 3 low-temp draws), embed with NLEmbedding, deduplicate near-duplicates via token-Jaccard ≥ 0.6, then greedily pick 7 maximising a submodular facility-location / max-sum-dispersion objective (on-task relevance + λ · min-embedding-distance-to-chosen − filler/compound penalty) — all deterministic Swift post-processing except the four upstream FM draws.
result: Scored 0.234 on the full-30 greedy eval (0 wins / 0 ties / 29 losses vs Sonnet), a catastrophic regression of −0.175 vs the champion adapter_v2a_e1 (0.409) and below the stock-3B baseline (0.282); coverage collapsed to 2 and nonRedundancy was crushed, with the judge unanimously flagging severe duplicate slots in nearly all 30 cases — the max-dispersion objective actively promoted paraphrase pairs that token-Jaccard dedup missed, confirming on-device embeddings are too coarse to measure clarifying-question dispersion. Discarded as the worst adapter-side configuration yet.
